answer: A farm emitting 153 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the timber panel. Because the entropy is measured at the dawn gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the sonnet audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 26 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
